title: A Friendship Without a Daily Message
title_ja: 毎日連絡しなくても続く友情
fact_notes: 人物・施設・活動・結果は架空の事例。実在の統計や研究結果ではない。個別の法律・工学手順の説明を目的としない。参考リンクは制作台帳であり、実証資料ではない。

sentences.en: When Lina and Grace began attending different universities, they promised to remain close friends despite living in separate cities.
sentences.ja: リナとグレースは別々の大学に通うようになったとき、違う都市に住んでも親友でいようと約束した。

sentences.en: For the first few weeks, they exchanged messages every evening and shared photographs of their new surroundings.
sentences.ja: 最初の数週間は毎晩メッセージを交わし、新しい環境の写真を共有した。

sentences.en: However, Grace soon began working several evenings a week, while Lina joined a club that required regular practice.
sentences.ja: しかしグレースはすぐに週に数晩働き始め、リナは定期的な練習が必要な部に入った。

sentences.en: Their conversations gradually became shorter, and sometimes neither person had enough time to respond until the following day.
sentences.ja: 会話は徐々に短くなり、翌日までどちらも返信する時間がないこともあった。

sentences.en: Lina worried that the decreasing frequency of their messages meant that the friendship was becoming less important to Grace.
sentences.ja: リナは連絡頻度の低下がグレースにとって友情の重要性が薄れていることを意味するのではと心配した。

sentences.en: Grace, on the other hand, assumed that her friend understood why her schedule had recently become more demanding.
sentences.ja: 一方グレースは最近予定が厳しくなった理由を友人が理解していると思っていた。

sentences.en: Neither of them had directly explained how the change in their communication had affected their expectations.
sentences.ja: どちらも連絡の変化が自分の期待にどう影響したか直接説明していなかった。

sentences.en: As a result, a practical scheduling problem gradually became a source of uncertainty about their relationship.
sentences.ja: その結果、実際には予定の問題だったものが徐々に関係への不安の原因となった。

sentences.en: During a weekend visit, Lina decided to describe her concerns without accusing Grace of deliberately ignoring her messages.
sentences.ja: 週末の訪問でリナは、グレースがわざと連絡を無視していると責めずに不安を伝えることにした。

sentences.en: Grace explained her working hours and admitted that she had sometimes felt guilty about being unable to reply immediately.
sentences.ja: グレースは勤務時間を説明し、すぐ返信できないことに罪悪感を覚える場合もあったと認めた。

sentences.en: The two friends realized that they had been treating the same delay as evidence of quite different things.
sentences.ja: 二人は同じ返信の遅れを、まったく異なることの証拠として捉えていたと気づいた。

sentences.en: They agreed that their existing arrangement no longer reflected the circumstances of their daily lives.
sentences.ja: これまでの取り決めが日常生活の状況に合わなくなったと合意した。

sentences.en: Instead of making another promise to communicate every day, they arranged a longer conversation on a mutually convenient evening each week.
sentences.ja: 毎日連絡する約束を再びする代わりに、週に一回双方に都合のよい夜に長めの会話をすることにした。

sentences.en: They could still send short messages whenever they wanted, but neither expected the other to respond within a particular period.
sentences.ja: いつでも短いメッセージを送れたが、相手に一定時間内の返信を期待しないことにした。

sentences.en: They also agreed to explain major changes in their availability rather than expect the other person to understand automatically.
sentences.ja: 相手が自動的に理解すると期待せず、連絡可能な時間に大きな変化があれば説明することにも合意した。

sentences.en: The new arrangement gave both friends more freedom while preserving a regular opportunity to share important experiences.
sentences.ja: 新しい取り決めは重要な経験を共有する定期的な機会を保ちつつ、双方により多くの自由を与えた。

sentences.en: The experience did not teach Lina and Grace that frequent communication was unnecessary in every friendship.
sentences.ja: その経験は、頻繁な連絡がすべての友情で不要だと教えたわけではない。

sentences.en: It reminded them that the meaning of a communication habit depends partly on the expectations shared by the people involved.
sentences.ja: 連絡の習慣の意味は関係する人々が共有する期待にも左右されることを思い出させた。

sentences.en: A relationship may change in form without necessarily becoming weaker, provided that both people remain willing to discuss their needs.
sentences.ja: 両者が互いの必要性を話し合う意思を持てば、関係は形を変えても必ずしも弱くならない場合がある。

sentences.en: For the two friends, maintaining their friendship meant adapting their habits rather than measuring affection by the number of messages exchanged.
sentences.ja: 二人にとって友情を維持するとは、メッセージ数で愛情を測るのでなく習慣を調整することだった。

questions.prompt: What change occurred in the friends' lives?
options: They moved into the same apartment.
They began attending different universities.
They both stopped working and studying.
They canceled every plan to stay in touch.

questions.prompt: Why did their conversations become shorter?
options: One friend lost every photograph.
Their universities prohibited messages.
They had agreed never to communicate again.
Their schedules became busier.
questions.explanation_ja: 双方の予定が忙しくなった。

questions.prompt: How did Lina interpret the decrease in messages?
options: She believed Grace had moved back home.
She knew Grace wanted more daily conversations.
She feared the friendship mattered less to Grace.
She regarded the change as entirely unimportant.
questions.explanation_ja: 友情の重要性の低下を心配した。

options: Lina understood why her schedule was demanding.
Lina had stopped attending university.
Lina wanted to end the friendship.
Lina knew the exact time of every shift.
questions.explanation_ja: 忙しい理由を分かっていると思った。

questions.prompt: Why did Lina avoid accusing Grace?
options: She had already decided that Grace was dishonest.
She did not want to learn about Grace's situation.
She planned to stop all conversations that day.
She wanted to express her feelings without assuming deliberate neglect.
questions.explanation_ja: 意図的な無視と決めつけずに気持ちを伝えた。

questions.prompt: What did Grace sometimes feel about late replies?
options: Proud.
Guilty.
Relieved that the friendship had ended.
Unconcerned about the delay.
questions.explanation_ja: 罪悪感を覚えることがあった。

questions.prompt: What new arrangement did they make?
options: A longer conversation on a convenient evening each week.
A fixed daily deadline for every message.
A complete ban on short messages.
A promise to meet in person every evening.
questions.explanation_ja: 週1回長めに話すことにした。

questions.prompt: What did they agree to explain to each other?
options: Every minor event during every day.
The exact number of messages sent to others.
Major changes in their availability.
The reasons for every university rule.
questions.explanation_ja: 連絡可能な時間の大きな変化を伝える。

options: A fixed deadline for communication.
Fondness or caring for another person.
The number of free evenings in a week.
A requirement to answer every message.
The strongest friendships always require daily messages.
A delayed reply necessarily proves that friendship is fading.
Friends should never discuss changes in their schedules.
Friends can sustain a relationship by adjusting habits and discussing expectations.
questions.explanation_ja: 期待を共有し習慣を調整することが友情を支える。

paraphrases.explanation_ja: 相互に話し合う意思があれば関係の形を変えられる。
